content.name: Sky toolkit v0 (programmable luminous constellations)
content.lineage: Shares the Micro-energy circuit toolkit's AtomDynamics vocabulary (the 'micro-electric' kit), lifted into the SKY at civic scale. It is the celestial pole of the Underground toolkit: the Underground programs the immutable substrate BENEATH the city; the Sky programs freely-authored constellations ABOVE it, legible from everywhere. See [[space:l2:mind-universe:underground-toolkit-v0]].

parent_scope.justification: Portable bootstrap toolkit awaiting installation under the canonical civic/physicalization registry Space. Exactly one scope classification; no PART_OF edge is written to an unbuilt parent.

content.native_law_boundary: AtomDynamics knows only AtomSpec, AtomBond and support/inhibit/neutral. The Sky is a physicalization grammar over that law: it renders and runs an atom circuit as a luminous constellation. It adds no predicate meaning; luminosity is a rendering of measured support energy, and what any given constellation MEANS is supplied by its author as data, never hard-coded in the toolkit.
content.purpose: Program anything, in the sky, via atoms. An author composes an atom circuit — AtomSpecs (thresholds, seeds, required-support AND-gates, inhibition) and AtomBonds (support / inhibit / neutral) — and the Sky toolkit physicalizes it as a constellation of luminous, interconnected stars and RUNS it: stars light when their measured support meets threshold, luminosity conducts along the lines once, the constellation settles at quiescence. Any behaviour expressible as AtomDynamics — a computation, a process, a loop, an orientation myth, a city's constitution — becomes a constellation overhead. The atom law is general (thresholds + AND-gates + inhibition + conduction), so the sky is a general programming surface, not a fixed picture.

programming_contract.star: one atom of the authored program, physicalized as a luminous point; brightness = its measured support energy
programming_contract.constellation_line: one AtomBond, physicalized as a line of light; support = warm/pressurised, inhibit = cold/severing, neutral = drawn but dark (carries 0)
programming_contract.constellation: the whole authored atom circuit, rendered AND run as a settling field of light
programming_contract.expressive_power: thresholds, required-support AND-gates, inhibition, one-shot conduction, starvation, quiescence — the full AtomDynamics law; any program in that law is authorable in the sky

examples.constitution: articles as stars, constitutional relations as lines, the founding article as a Pole Star above the civic-origin beacon — ONE application, not the toolkit's definition
examples.process: steps as stars that light in order along support lines
examples.guard: an inhibition line that keeps a star dark until a condition clears

programming_contract.rule: A star shines only when its support is present and MEASURED; an atom below threshold is dim and an unmeasured one is Fog (dark), never a fabricated bright star. Authoring or altering a constellation is an attributable act through the authoring port; a mere observer looking up never mutates the sky.

content.success_condition: For any authored atom program, the Sky toolkit renders it as a constellation and runs it faithfully: every star's brightness is its MEASURED support, every line is a real AtomBond, conduction happens once per bond, energy is conserved, and the field reaches quiescence. An atom below threshold is dim and an unmeasured one is Fog — never a fabricated bright star. The rendered-and-run constellation always matches the committed atom circuit, and no observer gesture mutates it.

content.pattern: A bounded Sky dome vaults over the city and carries no energy of its own. The author supplies an atom circuit; each atom physicalizes as a Star (roleAxis follows the atom's role: actor = a seeded source/Pole Star, narrative = an attractor that holds light, thing = a router). Each AtomBond physicalizes as a Constellation line that conducts luminosity once when its source star first fires. A star's brightness is a faithful render of its MEASURED support; below threshold it is dim, unmeasured it is Fog. The whole program is not just drawn but RUN: run_until_quiescent lights the reachable stars and settles the field. Access is split: anyone on the ground may READ and trace the constellation; authoring or altering it is an attributable act through the authoring port.
content.epistemic_honesty: A bright star is a measured-supported atom, not a wished-for one. A drawn line is a committed bond, not decoration. A dark region is Fog — an unmeasured or sub-threshold atom — never confident light. Looking up is not authoring; the sky is unreachable from the ground.

terms.SkyDome: The bounded Space that vaults over one city; roleAxis space, carries no energy, bounds the constellation.
terms.Star: One atom of the authored program, physicalized as a luminous point. Brightness = measured support energy; it shines only at or above its threshold.
terms.ConstellationLine: One AtomBond, physicalized as a line of light; polarity colours it (support warm, inhibit cold, neutral dark/zero). Exists iff the bond exists.
terms.Constellation: A whole authored atom circuit, rendered AND run as a settling field of light — a program made of stars.
terms.PoleStar: A convention, not a requirement: a seeded actor-roleAxis star an author may seat above the civic-origin beacon as an orientation anchor (e.g. a constitution's founding article).
terms.Luminosity: The rendered brightness of a star = its measured support energy. Never invented; unmeasured support renders as Fog.
terms.Program: The authored atom circuit (AtomSpecs + AtomBonds) that a constellation physicalizes and runs.
terms.Fire: A star's first transition when its support meets threshold, its required supports are all received, and it is not inhibited; it then conducts once along its outgoing lines.
terms.Fog: An unmeasured, unknown or sub-threshold atom; rendered as dark sky, never as a bright star.
terms.AuthoringPort: The mutation surface of the sky: authoring or altering a constellation. Attributable; a mere observer holds none of its capabilities.
terms.Constitution: ONE example program — articles as stars, constitutional relations as lines — not the toolkit's definition.

content.given: An authored atom circuit (AtomSpecs + AtomBonds), measured support/seed energies, an optional Pole-Star seat on the civic-origin axis, a visual catalog, and the acting actor's capability set.
content.when: The runtime renders and runs the constellation, an observer looks up to read or trace it, or an author mutates it (add/supersede a star, draw/sever a line).
then: Physicalize the atom circuit as a constellation: one Star per atom, one Constellation line per bond.
Run it: run_until_quiescent — light each star whose measured support meets threshold, conduct luminosity once along each line, settle at quiescence.
Render each star's brightness as a faithful projection of its MEASURED support; below threshold dim, unmeasured Fog.
Serve every read as observe-only: the observer sees stars, lines, brightness and conduction, and is offered no authoring affordance.
Resolve every mutation against the required authoring capability; admit only for an actor that holds it.
Fail an unauthorized mutation closed, leave the sky exactly as it was, and emit a rejection receipt.
forbidden: reading predicate names inside the native AtomDynamics law
rendering a sub-threshold, unknown or not_measured atom as a bright star (fabricated luminosity)
drawing a Constellation line where no AtomBond exists
conducting a line more than once
streaming authored, derived, unknown or not_measured luminosity
offering authoring affordances to an actor without the authoring capability
letting the act of looking up widen an actor's capability
moving a seated Pole Star off the civic-origin axis so sky and ground disagree on zero
presenting a renderer twinkle as a committed firing
silently dropping an unauthorized mutation instead of failing it closed with a receipt

steps: read the authored atom circuit (AtomSpecs + AtomBonds) and per-atom measured support
admit only measured support/seed energy through the membrane
optionally seat the Pole Star (a seeded actor atom) on the civic-origin axis
run_until_quiescent: fire each star meeting threshold + required supports + not inhibited
conduct luminosity once along each outgoing line (support adds light, inhibit severs, neutral zero)
hold sub-threshold and unmeasured atoms as Fog
repeat waves until the constellation settles (quiescence)
verify admitted integer luminosity is conserved
for a read: resolve the observe-only affordance set and render brightness without inventing luminosity
for a mutation: resolve the required authoring capability, admit only if held, else fail closed and leave the sky unchanged
emit the commit or rejection receipt
run the independent observer and the structured evaluation AST
derive health from fresh validation evidence
content.capability_resolution: read -> observe-only-set; authoring_port -> require(authoring_capability). No affordance escalates capability; an absent capability fails closed, never a silent mutation.
content.scheduler_projection: deterministic-wave-ticks/1; exact same-tick tie semantics must be reconciled with the canonical Rust crate when integrated.

content.authority: Graph-native CodeDefinition projection for the portable Sky toolkit; this JSON file is a materialized projection, not independent semantic authority.

authoring_gate.rule: A mutation (add/supersede star, draw/sever line) is admitted only when the acting capability set contains authority:sky-authoring. Looking up grants none of it.

atom_program.note: GENERIC: the atoms/bonds below are an illustrative program (a two-star support chain seeded by a Pole Star). A real constellation supplies ANY atom circuit at author time; the toolkit hard-codes no particular program — the star_circuit shape is the whole expressive surface.

content.honesty: The portable Sky toolkit is materialized and structurally shaped as a construct. This field is written BEFORE injection; after an injector commits it, the on-disk graph carries the construct while this embedded field reads stale (WRITTEN but not wired, executed, or proven healthy). No constellation is rendered and no program is run yet.

why: The sky is the one surface visible from everywhere in a city, so a program raised into it becomes a shared, orient-able reference — whatever the program is.

Driving the sky from the general AtomDynamics law (thresholds, AND-gates, inhibition, conduction) keeps it a genuine programming surface: any behaviour in that law is authorable, so the toolkit is not a fixed picture of one thing (a constitution) but an open medium.
Making brightness the render of MEASURED support means the sky cannot flatter a program: an unsupported atom stays dark, so aspiration and fact stay distinguishable at a glance.
Rendering AND running (not just drawing) means the constellation shows real dynamics — what lights what, what a guard inhibits — instead of a static diagram.
Keeping authoring attributable through a port, while reads stay open to all, mirrors the Underground's capability discipline above the city instead of below it.
rejected: hard-coding the constitution as the sky's meaning, because the toolkit must program anything the atom law can express, not one application
brightness from authored or wished-for status, because that would let the sky show light an atom never measured
decorative constellation lines with no bond, because a line that means nothing turns the sky into ornament
letting any observer edit the sky, because authoring must stay attributable
floating-point luminosity, because the canonical law counts conserved integer energy
health inferred from a twinkling renderer, because animation is not a firing

negative_invariants: neutral bond with nonzero energy rejected
authoring affordance offered to non-author rejected
invariants: any valid atom circuit renders and runs as a constellation
a star shines only with measured support at or above threshold
a Constellation line exists iff its AtomBond exists
an AND-gate star fires only when every required support conducted
every line conducts at most once
not_measured support renders as Fog, never as brightness
every authoring affordance resolves to the authoring capability
looking up never changes the acting capability set
an unauthorized mutation fails closed and leaves the sky unchanged

tests: detect a bright star whose atom has no measured support (fabricated luminosity)
detect a Constellation line with no committed AtomBond
detect a star that fired without all required supports
detect an inhibition line that failed to keep its star dark
detect an authoring affordance offered to an actor without the capability
detect a read that widened capability
detect an unauthorized mutation that changed the sky
detect an unauthorized mutation dropped without a rejection receipt
detect forged final luminosity or non-conserved energy
detect a missing or invalid receipt
never convert an unmeasured atom into a bright star

content.independence: Reads the authored atom circuit, per-atom measured support, the physicalized star event trace, final star states, the civic-origin beacon pose (for a seated Pole Star), the acting capability set, each resolved affordance, the commit/rejection receipt and the catalog. It does not trust a runtime-declared health field, a renderer twinkle, or an implementation self-report of firing.
checks: every star's brightness matches its measured support (no fabricated luminosity)
every Constellation line corresponds to a committed AtomBond
no committed bond is missing its line
AND-gate fire preconditions (all required supports conducted)
inhibition correctly keeps a star dark
a seated Pole Star aligns with the civic-origin beacon
every authoring affordance requires the authoring capability
read affordance sets contain observe-only capabilities
looking up leaves the acting capability set unchanged
unauthorized mutation failed closed and left the sky unchanged

derivation.healthy: All required fresh validation scenarios pass: any authored program rendered and ran faithfully, every star's brightness matched its measured support, every line matched a committed bond, AND-gates and inhibition behaved, luminosity was conserved and conducted once per line, a seated Pole Star aligned with the civic origin, authoring was capability-gated, and no unmeasured atom was rendered bright.
derivation.degraded: Fresh evidence exists but at least one non-catastrophic dimension violates its bound.
derivation.stale: The latest otherwise valid evidence exceeds the configured freshness window.
derivation.unknown: Required evidence cannot be resolved to a known state.
derivation.not_measured: No fresh validation run has measured the required dimensions.
derivation.measurement_failed: The observer or evaluator failed to produce a trustworthy measurement.

content.name: Sky authoring port (constellation mutation)
content.note: Reading the sky (from anywhere on the ground) is a separate observe-only surface; this port is the ONLY authoring surface and it requires the sky-authoring capability.
